2027-05-20.title: Thursday of the Seventh Week in Ordinary Time · St Bernardine of Siena
readings: Do not delay to turn back to the Lord
Blessed are they who hope in the Lord
It is better for you to enter life maimed than to have two hands and to go to hell
2027-05-20.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 7 (Year I). Ordinary Time resumed on the Monday after Pentecost; the Angelus has again taken the place of the Regina Caeli, and the Paschal candle now stands by the baptismal font. Liturgical colour: green. Optional memorial: St Bernardine of Siena, priest (white). In some countries the bishops have adopted, on this Thursday after Pentecost, the feast of Our Lord Jesus Christ, the Eternal High Priest; it is not assumed here for India.
2027-05-20.verse: Do not delay to turn back to the Lord, and do not postpone it from day to day.
theo: Ben Sira today writes a list of things we must never say. “Do not rely on your wealth, or say, ‘I have enough.’” “Do not say, ‘Who can have power over me?’” “Do not say, ‘I sinned, yet what has happened to me?’ for the Lord is slow to anger.” Each sentence names a false security. Money that makes us think we need nobody, strength that makes us think we answer to nobody, and, most subtle of all, a kind of presumption on God's patience: nothing happened when I sinned, so it cannot matter. Ben Sira goes further: “Do not be so confident of forgiveness that you add sin to sin. Do not say, ‘His mercy is great, he will forgive the multitude of my sins.’” God's mercy is real and vast, but it is the mercy of a holy God, never permission to keep sinning. And so the urgent counsel: “Do not delay to turn back to the Lord, and do not postpone it from day to day.” The sinner always means to repent tomorrow. Ben Sira asks: why not today? The Psalm paints the two ways: the one who delights in the law of the Lord is “like trees planted by streams of water,” while the wicked are “like chaff that the wind drives away.”

The Gospel continues the teaching Jesus gave at Capernaum. It opens with a promise so small it is easy to miss: “whoever gives you a cup of water to drink because you bear the name of Christ will by no means lose the reward.” No kindness done for Christ is ever wasted. Then the tone becomes severe. To cause one of “these little ones who believe” to stumble is so grave that a millstone around the neck would be better. Jesus speaks of cutting off a hand or a foot, tearing out an eye, rather than being thrown into “hell, where their worm never dies, and the fire is never quenched.” The Church has never taken this as a command to injure the body; it is the vivid language of a teacher who wants us to see that nothing, not even what is dearest to us, is worth losing eternal life for. Whatever leads us into sin, a habit, a phone, a friendship, a place, must be cut away decisively. And he ends with salt: “Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.” Today the Church remembers St Bernardine of Siena (1380–1444), the Franciscan who preached across Italy with this same urgency, calling crowds to conversion and teaching them to love the Holy Name of Jesus. He did not let people postpone; he told them that today is the day.
outline: Ask: what am I planning to change “tomorrow”?
Point 1 · Do not say “I have enough”
False securities: wealth, strength, presumption on mercy.
Conversion belongs to today, not tomorrow.
Point 3 · A cup of water and the salt of peace
Cut away what makes us stumble; no kindness for Christ is lost.
“Do not delay to turn back to the Lord.”
live: Name one sin or habit you keep postponing, and take one concrete step against it before tonight; if needed, plan your confession for this week.
Offer a drink, a meal or a kind word today to someone who serves the Church or the poor.
2027-05-20.prayer: Holy and merciful God, you are slow to anger and rich in mercy; do not let us presume on your patience. Give us the grace to turn back to you today, without delay, and to cut away whatever leads us into sin. Through the prayers of St Bernardine, who preached the Holy Name of Jesus with burning love, write that name on our hearts, so that we may have salt in ourselves and be at peace with one another. Amen.
altar: The mercy Ben Sira warns us not to presume upon is offered to us in its fullness at the altar, where Christ's Body is given and his Blood is poured out “for the forgiveness of sins.” To receive him worthily is to turn back to the Lord today; and every Communion sends us out with salt, to be peacemakers.

quick: Ben Sira: do not trust in wealth or strength, and do not presume on God's mercy to keep sinning.
Do not delay to turn back to the Lord; do not put it off from day to day.
Jesus: a cup of water given in his name is rewarded; cut off whatever causes you to sin; have salt and be at peace.
2027-05-20.action: Take one concrete step today against a sin you keep postponing.
2027-05-20.question: Which conversion have I been putting off until tomorrow?
kidsaint: Bernardine lived in Italy six hundred years ago. When he was twenty, a terrible sickness came to his city, and he and his friends looked after the sick in the hospital day and night. Later he became a Franciscan preacher and travelled from town to town. He carried a board with the letters IHS, the first letters of the name of Jesus in Greek, shining like the sun, and taught everyone to love that holy name. Lesson: say the name of Jesus with love many times a day.

family.explain: Jesus says that even a cup of water given to someone because they belong to him will never be forgotten by God. Small kind things matter to Jesus. He also says that if something makes us do wrong again and again, we must throw it away, like a bad habit.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who needs to come back to God, and for people who have no clean drinking water.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there one bad habit our family should stop starting from today? What small kindness can we do instead?”

illus: A story told about St Bernardine: after one of his sermons against gambling, people in a city burned their dice and playing cards in the square. A man who made playing cards for a living came to him in distress: you have ruined my trade. Bernardine is said to have drawn the sign of the Holy Name, the letters IHS surrounded by rays of the sun, and told him to make and sell that instead. The man did, and the tablets of the Holy Name spread through Italy. Whether every detail is exact or not, the point is sound: conversion does not only remove what is bad; it makes room for something better.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, we do not want to delay any longer. Turn our hearts to you today. Amen.
share: Do not rely on your wealth, or say, “I have enough” (Sirach 5:1). Where do I feel I do not need God?
Do not delay to turn back to the Lord (Sirach 5:7). What conversion have I been postponing?
Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another (Mark 9:50). With whom do I need to make peace?
pm.resp: Blessed are they who hope in the Lord.
interc: For all who keep putting off their return to God, that they may hear his call today.
For those who are led into sin by others, and for the little ones who have been scandalised.
For preachers of the Gospel, that like St Bernardine they may call people to conversion with love.
For families and communities divided by quarrels, that they may be at peace with one another.
For our group, that we may give a cup of water to all who serve in Christ's name.
pm.close: Father, you are patient with sinners and you wait for our return. Make us turn to you today, through Jesus, whose name is above every name. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, there is one word the devil loves: tomorrow. I will pray tomorrow. I will go to confession next month. I will forgive my brother after he apologises. Ben Sira knew this temptation well, and he says today: do not delay to turn back to the Lord, and do not postpone it from day to day (Sirach 5:7).

He also warns us against sentences we say inside. I have enough. Who can control me? I sinned and nothing happened. God is merciful, he will forgive anything. Yes, God is merciful, wonderfully merciful. But his mercy is meant to lead us to repentance, not to give us permission to add sin to sin.

In the Gospel Jesus uses very strong words. If your hand, your foot, your eye causes you to sin, cut it off. He does not want us to harm our bodies. He wants us to be serious. If a mobile phone, a bottle, a bad friendship or a habit keeps pulling me into sin, I must cut it off decisively. Nothing is worth more than eternal life.

But Jesus also says something very gentle: whoever gives you a cup of water because you bear the name of Christ will by no means lose the reward (Mark 9:41). Today we remember St Bernardine of Siena, who preached conversion across Italy and taught people to love the Holy Name of Jesus. Let us take his advice: say the name of Jesus often, turn to him today, not tomorrow, and be at peace with one another. Amen.
kids: Children, sometimes we say: I will say sorry tomorrow, I will clean my room later, I will pray next time. The Bible says: do not wait! Turn to God today. And Jesus says that even giving a cup of water to someone with love makes God happy. Can you say sorry and do a small kindness today?

intro: Theme: “Do not delay to turn back to the Lord.”
False securities, the danger of tomorrow, and the salt of a heart converted today.

q: Do not be so confident of forgiveness that you add sin to sin.
Or do you despise the riches of his kindness and forbearance and patience? Do you not realize that God's kindness is meant to lead you to repentance?
points.apply: Write down one false security you lean on, and give it to God in prayer.

sub: Cut off what makes you stumble.
Nothing is worth losing life for.
q: Do not delay to turn back to the Lord, and do not postpone it from day to day.
See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation!
points.apply: Make your confession this week, or take one decisive step away from an occasion of sin.

points.h: A cup of water and the salt of peace
sub: No kindness for Christ is lost.
Do not scandalise the little ones.
Salt and peace with one another.
q: Depart from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it.
Salt is good; but if salt has lost its saltiness, how can you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.
points.apply: Make peace this week with one person from whom you are estranged.

concl: God's patience is not permission; it is an invitation to turn back today.
A heart that turns to Christ cuts away what leads to sin, gives cups of water in his name, and lives at peace.
2027-05-20.resolve: Say the name of Jesus with love each hour today, as St Bernardine taught, and turn to him without delay.
